parole.testo: From Dutch bui or Low German bö, böe, böje. Cognate with Danish byge, Norwegian Bokmål byge, bøye and Norwegian Nynorsk bye, bøye.
Borrowed from Dutch gieren (“to yaw”) or Low German giren. First attested in 1690. Cognate of German gieren (“to yaw”), Danish gire, and Norwegian geira (“go wrong”).

parole.significato: To have enough strength, will, or stamina for something.
parole.testo: Affix of pall + -ar, from stå pall (“stand firm”). Borrowed from Dutch pal staan, from Low German pall staan. Interjection sense possibly an ellipsis of the negative pallar inte ("do not have energy/stamina/will").

parole.significato: to manage to withstand stresses; to hold up, to stand up, to stand firm, etc.
parole.testo: Compound of stå (“stand”) + pall (“catch; stopping mechanism”). Borrowed from Dutch pal staan (“stand firm”), from Low German pall staan.
